questions.answer: No conflict. Every AHB read, including INCR4/8/16 and WRAP4/8/16, issues one single-beat AXI read (ARLEN=0) for each accepted beat. Reads are never aggregated.

The documents conflict. FEAT-004 is 'Required', and 5.3 says the bridge 'emit[s] one matching INCR/WRAP AXI burst' when attributes are constant. REQ-FUNC-005 and 1.1 say 'may', which T1 defines as optional. The designer must decide whether aggregation is mandatory whenever the conditions hold.

Early OKAY for non-final, safely buffered beats is permitted ('may'), not required. A later B error is reported only on the terminal AHB beat, and the terminal beat waits for the required B response(s). Earlier buffered beats stay acknowledged.

A burst is aggregated only when it is a complete, legal bufferable Normal Write-back fixed burst (4/8/16) whose AXI address attributes are constant, and only after all beats are captured. Otherwise it uses ordered singles. Device-E and non-bufferable writes are always singles. The 4 KiB split is only defensive, for an out-of-profile address sequence that crosses 4 KiB. A compliant AHB burst does not need it.

Reset clears all bridge and FIFO valid state. In-flight commands, data and responses are discarded and the AXI VALIDs drop. No pre-reset response may be returned after release, provided the connected AXI endpoint or interconnect is reset consistently.

The text is inconsistent on whether the 6-cycle limit is a hard bound or a goal. REQ-PERF-002 says 'shall meet', but 10.4 and 13 call it a 'target', and 13 marks it 'requires implementation verification'. The designer must say whether a miss fails a check. The count starts at the accepted AHB address, so earlier AHB stall cycles are not counted. The conditions are queue space and AXI READY high.

EXOKAY is 'unexpected' because no exclusive accesses are issued, so every EXOKAY is treated as an error and maps to AHB ERROR. The required BRESPs are one per AXI write transaction issued. That is one for an aggregated burst, one per sub-burst if split, and one per beat for ordered singles.

PARA_RD_ID_COUNT and PARA_WR_ID_COUNT are the only parameters. Both have default 1 and legal range 1..8. Out-of-range values are elaboration errors. The text does not say how the error is raised (generate-time $error or otherwise).

The text says at most one read and one write are outstanding, but it does not say whether both can be outstanding at once. 10.4 says no later transaction bypasses an unresolved operation, 'when required'. Early OKAY on buffered writes may let a later read start while a write B is pending. The designer must state whether read and write are fully serialized.
Earlier buffered beats stay acknowledged with OKAY. The B error is reported on the terminal AHB beat, which reflects the status of all B responses.

Release synchronization is a SoC integration assumption, and the bridge has no reset synchronizer. Asynchronous assertion is part of the contract and must be verified. During reset, HREADYOUT=1, HRESP=OKAY, AW/W/ARVALID=0 and BREADY/RREADY=0, and in-flight state is dropped.
Yes. Both interfaces use the single i_clk_core domain, with no CDC. The English text is normative and the Vietnamese text restates the same intent for review, so it is not an independent requirement.

VALID and payload must stay stable until the READY handshake. The payload is only qualified by its VALID. Reset is the exception: it clears VALID and discards in-flight state, and the combinational adapter suppresses VALID during reset.
Yes. Any accepted transfer with HMASTLOCK=1 is rejected with a two-cycle AHB ERROR and no AXI request. The reset/idle value of 0 only applies to the idle input state.

A 1 KiB-crossing burst is out-of-profile stimulus: the manager must not start it. The 4 KiB split is a defensive behavior that does not make such a burst compliant. It is still a tested scenario (TEST-08, WF-006).

ID counts are per direction and set by the static parameters PARA_RD_ID_COUNT and PARA_WR_ID_COUNT, range 1..8. Each direction rotates through 0..count-1 after each completed AXI transaction. There is no conflict, because a count above 1 does not enable concurrent transactions. The ID is checked against the configured count (15.3). The text does not specify at which handshake it is checked, and it leaves a mismatched response ID undefined.

The two statements do not conflict. Aggregation is optional ('may'), but its precondition is that the full burst is captured and the attributes are uniform. An incomplete or early-terminated burst is never sent as an AXI burst. Its captured, unissued beats go out as ordered singles, and the terminal AHB response carries the aggregated B status.

Writes are single-beat by default, with bursts up to 16 beats as the exception. Only complete, legal, bufferable Normal Write-back fixed bursts (INCR/WRAP 4/8/16, HPROT[6:2]=0b0_x111) with constant AXI address attributes may be bursts. Device, non-cacheable, write-through and non-bufferable writes stay single-beat.
There is no limit and no internal timeout. If R or B never arrives, the AHB operation waits indefinitely. Recovery belongs to a system watchdog or reset.

The supported errors are those in §12. These are AXI non-OKAY responses (SLVERR, DECERR, unexpected EXOKAY) and locally rejected transfers (HMASTLOCK, HPROT[6]=1 or unsupported HPROT, HSIZE>2, misalignment, reserved HBURST). Each is returned as a two-cycle AHB ERROR (HRESP=1), with no split response.

Verification must be independent of RTL internals. It should check reset clearing through the interface: no traffic during reset, queues empty in effect, and no stale response after release. It should not use hierarchical probes.

Acceptance is an AHB notion: at a rising i_clk_core edge with HSEL, HREADY and HTRANS[1] all 1. No transfer is accepted until reset release. The text does not name a specific first cycle after release beyond that.

The ID range is stated: 3-bit ID, rotation through 0..count-1 per direction. The documents do not give the reset or initial ID value, nor the explicit wrap order for a count that is not a power of 2. The designer must state both.
Same as Q7: out-of-range parameter values are elaboration errors.
Yes. The counts are static elaboration parameters (1..8, default 1), set independently for read and write. Each direction rotates through IDs 0..count-1 after each completed AXI transaction.
HSIZE>2 (larger sizes) is rejected with a two-cycle AHB ERROR. Nothing is forwarded to AXI for the rejected transfer, and any earlier accepted write prefix is drained.
The documents give only pre-split lengths (LEN 3, 7 or 15). They do not say how a split burst divides into sub-burst lengths. The designer must define the AWLEN of each sub-burst.
Same as Q5. The hard-bound versus target ambiguity is open. Device-E writes are issued as AXI singles, but the text does not state that the 6-cycle bound applies to them.

Yes. During reset AW/W/ARVALID=0, BREADY/RREADY=0, HREADYOUT=1 and HRESP=OKAY. In-flight queues and VALID state are dropped, so in-flight write data is discarded. No stale response appears after release if the AXI endpoint is reset consistently.

'Eligible' means a complete, legal, bufferable Normal Write-back fixed write burst (INCR/WRAP 4/8/16, HPROT[6:2]=0b0_x111 with HPROT[2]=1) whose burst-scoped AXI address attributes stay constant. 'Varying' means a burst-scoped AXI address attribute differs between accepted beats, which causes a fallback to ordered singles.
No AXI request is issued for the rejected beat. Any accepted write prefix is drained before the terminal response, and the terminal response waits for all relevant B responses.
The terminal AHB beat always reports the error. Statuses from all B responses (single, split or fallback) are aggregated onto it. Earlier beats may already have returned OKAY.
Yes. Since no exclusives are issued, EXOKAY is unexpected and treated as an error for both reads and writes. It maps to a two-cycle AHB ERROR.

Measurement runs from the accepted AHB address (HSEL, HREADY and HTRANS[1] all 1) to the AR/AW handshake. The §10.4 conditions are that the synchronous queue has space and the corresponding AXI READY stays high. For fixed-length write bursts the clock starts after full capture or early termination.
The AXI interface instance is u_ahb2axi_axi_if. m_ahb2axi_ctrl is the module name and u_ahb2axi_ctrl is its instance in m_ahb2axi_top, so there is no conflict. The top module is m_ahb2axi_top.

The FIFO contract (interface, depth, reset behavior) is delegated to the external 002_SyncFIFO spec (REF-004), which is not in these documents. The text does not say how a violation of that contract is detected. The designer must specify the FIFO contract checks.

The reset is asserted asynchronously. VALID/READY are suppressed combinationally by the reset in the AXI adapter, so VALID is low while reset is asserted and is not waiting for a clock edge. The sequential state is also cleared asynchronously.

Complete means all data beats of the fixed AHB burst are captured, or the burst's early termination is captured. AW may be issued only after that. No AW may be issued before the complete aggregated burst.
The configured ID counts are the static elaboration parameters PARA_RD_ID_COUNT and PARA_WR_ID_COUNT. They are not ports or registers, so the bound is checked against the elaborated parameter values.

It is a statement of fact, because there is a single clock domain and no CDC. Asynchronous clock groups and false paths between bridge logic and FIFO pointers are prohibited. Only constraints with a basis from the selected library and SoC flow are allowed, so that flow supplies the justification.
Yes. Each is rejected with a two-cycle AHB ERROR and no AXI request for the rejected transfer.

§6.3 (T1.7.3.3) defines the mapping. HPROT[1] passes to AxPROT[0], HNONSEC to AxPROT[1], and ~HPROT[0] to AxPROT[2]. HPROT[3] maps to AxCACHE[1] and HPROT[2] to AxCACHE[0]. HPROT[4:5] set the direction-specific allocate bits. HPROT[6]=1 is rejected, and any HPROT[6:2] pattern not listed is reserved and returns ERROR. The listed supported patterns are 0b0_0000, 0b0_0001, 0b0_0010, 0b0_x110 and 0b0_x111.
Yes, they are the 1-bit AWLOCK and ARLOCK outputs, tied to 0. AXI3 is out of scope, so the AXI3 2-bit form does not apply.

It is measured from the accepted AHB address (HSEL, HREADY and HTRANS[1] all 1) to the AR/AW handshake, in i_clk_core cycles. For fixed write bursts it starts only after full-burst capture or early termination, so the first AHB address is not covered.

Eligible means Normal Write-back, HPROT[6:2]=0b0_x111, with HPROT[2] (bufferable) set, under the §6.3 mapping. For these, errors are reported at the terminal AHB beat. Device-E and non-bufferable writes wait for BRESP on each beat.
Same as Q18: AHB waits indefinitely with no internal timeout. TEST-07 covers it with delayed or missing R/B responses, asserting no completion bound.

Yes on both counts. 'Does not merge' means Device-E writes are never merged into an AXI burst and their size is not changed. They are issued as ordered AXI singles. 'Waits for BRESP' means the AHB completion is held until the final-destination BRESP arrives, with no early AHB response.
A read address is accepted at a rising i_clk_core edge when HSEL, HREADY and HTRANS[1] are all 1 (NONSEQ or SEQ). Only then may the AR be issued.
